title: Red Wine Beef Stew with Mashed Potatoes
facts: About 3–4 hours, guided by the tenderness of the beef
ingredientLines: 1 tin of tomato paste (156 ml per tin)
preparationGuidance: Use beef suitable for stewing, cut into 3–4 cm cubes. Start with 600–750 ml water and adjust during the braise. Use the cornstarch only if the gravy needs thickening. Add the measured seasoning gradually, to taste.
steps: Prep and brown. Pat the beef dry, season it with salt and generous black pepper, and brown it in batches in an oiled Dutch oven. Avoid crowding the pot. Transfer the beef to a plate. Cut the carrots and celery into a medium dice—½-inch (about 1.2 cm) cubes—so the pieces remain distinct in the finished stew. Dice the onions similarly.

Build the base and reserve the vegetables. Cook the onions, carrots and celery in the pot until the onions soften and the vegetables pick up a little colour. Lift out all the vegetables with a slotted spoon and set aside. Add minced garlic and tomato paste to the pot; stir for about 2 minutes. Pour in the wine, scrape up the browned bits (deglaze), and let the wine reduce for several minutes.

Start the braise (cook gently in a small amount of liquid). Return the beef and its juices to the pot. Add bay leaves, the bouillon cube, and enough water to almost cover the beef. Bring the liquid just to a light simmer: occasional small bubbles should break the surface, without a rolling boil. Cover, leaving the lid slightly ajar if needed to maintain that gentle movement.

Braise until nearly tender. Check the liquid occasionally and add a little hot water if it drops too far. Allow roughly 2½–3½ hours of gentle braising in total, but judge it by the beef: a fork should slide in easily. Different cuts will take different times; lean cuts can become drier even when tender.

Final 40 minutes. Return the reserved vegetables for the last 40 minutes of the braise so they soften while retaining some texture. Meanwhile, peel the potatoes and cut them into even chunks. Boil in salted water until a fork passes through easily, then drain thoroughly and mash with butter and warm milk.

Finish. Remove the bay leaves. If the gravy needs body, reduce it (simmer uncovered to concentrate it) briefly or add a cornstarch slurry (starch mixed with cold water) and simmer until glossy. Taste and adjust salt and black pepper.

title: Chicken Chickpea and Potato Coconut Curry with Rice
preparationGuidance:
Before you start: Soak and fully cook the listed 200 g dry chickpeas according to their package directions. Use the entire drained batch in this recipe; cooked yield varies. The meal time below excludes soaking and bean cooking. If preparing them ahead, cool promptly and refrigerate until needed.

Use chicken breast or boneless thigh, cut into bite-size pieces. Cook the dry chickpeas ahead as described below. Add 250–350 ml water to the curry; measure rice cooking water according to its package. Cilantro is an optional extra, not included in the shopping list.
steps: 0:00 — Start rice. Rinse rice and put it on with measured water and salt. Bring to a boil, cover, lower heat and cook per package; rest covered 10 minutes.

0:05–0:18 — Cut and sweat. Cut onion and carrots into a small dice (¼-inch, about 6 mm cubes). Cut potatoes into larger, roughly 1.5 cm cubes; cut chicken separately. Finely grate the ginger so it disperses and softens quickly. Sweat the onion and carrot (cook gently in oil without browning) for 5 minutes. Add garlic, ginger, curry powder, cumin, cloves, bay leaves, cinnamon and ground hot pepper; bloom the spices (stir them briefly in hot oil to release their aroma) for 1 minute.
0:18–0:35 — Simmer. Stir in potatoes, coconut milk and water. Cover and simmer 12–15 minutes, until potatoes are almost tender.

0:35–0:48 — Add chicken and beans. Add chicken and drained cooked chickpeas. Simmer 10–12 minutes, stirring, until chicken reaches 74°C and potato is tender. If using thigh chunks, allow a few more minutes.
Finish. Remove the bay leaves and visible cloves. Balance (adjust) with salt and lemon or lime, then spoon over rice.

title: Beet Turkey and Buckwheat Skillet
preparationGuidance: Peel and coarsely grate the beets; thinly shred the cabbage. Cook buckwheat with water according to its package. Yogurt is optional but included in the shopping list. Add salt and pepper to taste.
steps: 0:00–0:05 — Start buckwheat. Rinse and cook in salted water according to the package, generally 15–20 minutes; keep covered afterward.

0:05–0:18 — Prep. Cut onion into a small dice (¼-inch, about 6 mm cubes), finely shred the cabbage into thin ribbons, and coarsely grate the peeled beets on a box grater. Use a separate board for raw turkey.

0:18–0:28 — Brown turkey. Heat a large skillet with oil. Sauté (cook in a little hot oil while stirring) the turkey with onion, breaking it apart; season with salt, paprika and coriander. Cook until no pink remains and the turkey reaches 74°C.

0:28–0:43 — Cook vegetables. Add garlic, beets and cabbage plus 100 ml water. Cover for 7–9 minutes, then uncover and reduce (evaporate) the excess moisture. The beets should be tender with a little bite.
Finish. Stir in dill and lemon juice. Serve over buckwheat with yogurt mixed with lemon zest and a pinch of salt, if using.

title: Beef Mushroom and Pepper Stir-Fry with Rice
preparationGuidance: Use tender beef suitable for stir-frying, sliced thinly across the grain. The optional coating uses the white of the listed egg; save the yolk for another use. Use 100 ml water in the sauce and rice cooking water according to the package. Green onions are an optional extra, not included in the shopping list.
steps: 0:00 — Start rice according to package directions.

0:05–0:18 — Slice and mix. Cut the beef into an émincé (thin slices), across the grain so the muscle fibres are short. For a light protective coating, if desired, toss the beef with egg white and a little of the measured soy sauce and cornstarch before its brief sear. Slice onions, mushrooms and peppers. Mix remaining soy sauce, starch, vinegar, sugar and water in a cup.

0:18–0:34 — Stir-fry and sear. Sear means brown rapidly over high heat. Heat cast iron or stainless pan until hot. Sear beef in 2–3 batches, 2–3 minutes per batch; transfer out. Cook onions, mushrooms and peppers in batches so they brown rather than steam.

0:34–0:43 — Combine. Add garlic for 30 seconds. Return beef and juices, pour in the re-stirred sauce, and toss until the thickened sauce lightly coats the beef and vegetables. Check the beef with a food thermometer: at least 63°C for whole-cut beef, or longer for your preferred doneness. If using mechanically tenderized beef, follow the package’s cooking directions. Cook the optional egg-white coating through.
Finish. Serve over rice, adding green onions if wanted.

title: Chicken Peanut Pasta with Carrot and Spinach
preparationGuidance: Use chicken breast or boneless thigh, sliced. Julienne the carrots, slice the onion and mince the garlic. Reserve 200–300 ml hot pasta water for the sauce. Chili flakes are an optional extra, not included in the shopping list.
steps: 0:00–0:08 — Boil and cut. Put a large pot of salted water on high heat. Cut chicken into strips, julienne the carrots (thin matchsticks), slice the onion, and mince garlic (chop very finely).

0:08–0:22 — Cook in parallel. Boil pasta according to package, reserving a mug of its starchy cooking water to emulsify the sauce (help fat and water form a smooth mixture). In a wide pan, cook chicken in oil in two batches until browned and 74°C; set aside. Cook onion and carrots 5 minutes, then garlic 1 minute.
0:22–0:30 — Make sauce. Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, vinegar, honey and 200 ml hot pasta water until smooth. Add more water if needed; it should pour easily.

0:30–0:40 — Finish the pasta. Return chicken to the pan, add spinach to wilt, then add drained pasta and sauce. Toss over low heat until the sauce clings to the pasta; loosen with reserved water as needed. Adjust with water and lime or vinegar.
Finish. Taste for acidity and salt; add lime or vinegar if needed.

title: Rosemary Beef, Mushroom and Potato Casserole
facts: About 3–4 hours, mostly unattended; judge by the beef's tenderness
preparationGuidance: Cut beef into roughly 3 cm pieces and potatoes into 2–3 cm chunks. Slice mushrooms, cut onions into wedges and carrots on the bias. Use 125 ml water with the bouillon cube. Cornstarch is optional but included in the shopping list. Add salt and pepper to taste.
steps: Sear the beef. Heat a cast-iron or stainless-steel skillet with a little oil. Brown the beef in batches, seasoning with salt and pepper. Sear means to brown the surface quickly in a hot pan; the beef does not need to cook through. Transfer it directly into a large casserole baking dish.

Fill the casserole. Add mushrooms, onions, carrots, potatoes, garlic and rosemary to the dish. If using cornstarch, scatter it over the ingredients and toss thoroughly so no dry patches remain. Dissolve the bouillon cube in the 125 ml water and pour it in. Dot with butter and add a generous grind of black pepper. Toss once more and cover the dish tightly with its lid or foil.

Cook from a cold oven. Put the covered dish into the oven, then set it to 160°C; there is no need to preheat. Let it cook gently for roughly 3 hours before checking. This is a braise: the covered ingredients slowly cook in the small amount of added liquid plus moisture released by the vegetables. The sauce should barely bubble, not boil vigorously.

Check and finish. The beef is ready when a fork slides in easily, and the potatoes and carrots are tender. If necessary, cover and cook longer, checking periodically; the time will vary with the cut of beef and the dish's depth. Stir from the bottom, remove the rosemary stems, and taste for salt and pepper. The released vegetable juices should form a small amount of glossy sauce. If it is thinner than you like, uncover for the last 10–15 minutes.

title: Beef Black Bean and Chipotle Chili
ingredientLines: 1 tin of tomato paste (156 ml per tin)
preparationGuidance:
Before you start: Soak and fully cook the listed 200 g dry black beans according to their package directions. Use the entire drained batch in this recipe; cooked yield varies. The meal time below excludes soaking and bean cooking. If preparing them ahead, cool promptly and refrigerate until needed.

Cook the dry black beans ahead as described below. Blend or finely chop the tomatoes. Soften and mince the chipotles. Rice is optional but included in the shopping list; use cooking water according to its package. Add chili flakes and salt to taste.
steps: 0:00 — Start optional rice. Rinse and cook according to package. Put both chipotles in hot water to soften.
0:05–0:18 — Chop and brown. Cut onion, carrot and peppers into a small dice (¼-inch, about 6 mm cubes). Brown beef in a Dutch oven, breaking it up. Drain excess fat if necessary.

0:18–0:30 — Build flavour. Add onion and carrot for 6 minutes, then bell peppers and garlic for 4 minutes. Stir in minced chipotles, tomato paste, chili flakes and spices for 1 minute to bloom the spices (release their aroma in the hot fat).

0:30–0:50 — Simmer. Add blended fresh tomatoes and cooked black beans. Reduce (simmer uncovered to evaporate liquid), stirring occasionally, until thick enough to mound on a spoon. Add a splash of water only if it threatens to stick. Ground beef should reach 71°C.
Finish. Salt and add lime to taste. Serve as a thick chili or over rice.

title: Greek Chicken Bulgur Bowls with Dill Yogurt
preparationGuidance: Use chicken breast or boneless thigh. Cook bulgur with water according to its package. Divide the fresh dill between the yogurt sauce and vegetables. Add salt and pepper to taste.
steps: 0:00–0:10 — Start grain and sauce. Cook bulgur in salted water as directed. Stir yogurt with lemon juice, grated garlic, half the chopped dill and salt; refrigerate.

0:10–0:22 — Prep. Cut chicken into an émincé (even, thin strips); season with oregano, salt, pepper, oil and lemon zest. Dice the cucumber, tomatoes and pepper (cut into small, even cubes); toss with greens, remaining dill and a little olive oil.
0:22–0:35 — Sear. Sear means brown rapidly in a hot pan. Heat a wide skillet and cook chicken in batches, turning, until browned and 74°C. Rest 3 minutes.
0:35–0:45 — Finish. Fluff the bulgur with a fork. Serve with chicken, cool vegetables and dill yogurt sauce.

title: Chicken Mushroom and Dill Pilaf
preparationGuidance: Use chicken breast or boneless thigh. Rinse the rice and measure hot water according to its package, allowing for the tomato juice. Use only one point (one segment) from the whole star anise; keep the rest for another meal. Dice the tomatoes. Add ground hot pepper, salt and black pepper to taste.
steps: 0:00–0:15 — Prep. Rinse rice until water is mostly clear. Cut chicken into even bite-size pieces; cut onion and carrots into a medium dice (½-inch, about 1.2 cm cubes); slice mushrooms. Mince garlic (chop very finely) and dice tomatoes.

0:15–0:28 — Infuse and brown. Heat oil in a wide Dutch oven. Add the whole cloves and star-anise point for about 30 seconds to infuse the oil (release their aroma into the fat). Lift them out and reserve. Brown salted chicken in two batches; remove. Sauté (cook in a little oil while stirring) onion, carrot and mushrooms until the mushroom water has largely evaporated.

0:28–0:35 — Toast. Add garlic, paprika, cumin and ground hot pepper; bloom the ground spices (heat briefly in oil to release aroma) for 30 seconds. Stir in tomatoes and toast the rice (coat and heat the grains) for 2 minutes. Return chicken, its juices and the reserved whole spices.

0:35–0:53 — Steam. Add measured hot liquid and salt. Bring to a boil, cover tightly, lower heat and cook 15–18 minutes, until rice is tender and chicken reaches 74°C. Turn off heat and rest covered 5 minutes. Do not repeatedly lift the lid.

Finish. Find and remove the two cloves and star-anise point. Fluff with dill and black pepper. If your rice package specifies a different liquid ratio, use that ratio, accounting for the small amount of tomato juice.

title: Broccoli Shrimp and Pepper Noodles
preparationGuidance: Thaw the raw peeled shrimp if frozen. Use 150 ml water in the sauce and cooking water for the noodles. Sesame oil is optional but included in the shopping list. Ginger and chili are optional extras, not included in the shopping list.
steps: 0:00–0:12 — Boil and prep. Put noodle water on high heat. Cut broccoli into small florets and julienne the peeled stems (thin matchsticks); thinly slice peppers and green onions. Pat shrimp dry. Whisk soy sauce, vinegar, honey, starch and water.

0:12–0:22 — Cook noodles and vegetables. Cook noodles per package; drain. Stir-fry (cook quickly while moving the food in a hot pan) broccoli and peppers with a splash of water; cover 3 minutes, uncover and cook until bright and crisp-tender. Add garlic, ginger if using, and white green-onion parts.
0:22–0:29 — Cook shrimp. Push vegetables aside or work in batches. Cook shrimp until opaque and firm, generally 2–3 minutes per side depending on size; reach 74°C. Avoid prolonged cooking.
0:29–0:35 — Sauce. Re-stir the starch mixture, pour it into the pan and simmer until it thickens enough to lightly coat the vegetables. Toss with noodles, sesame oil and green onion tops.

title: Chicken Biryani with Boiled Eggs
facts: 2–3 hours including the minimum marinating time; overnight marinating is extra
preparationGuidance: Cut chicken thighs into large pieces and slice the onions thinly. Use dry basmati rice. Crack the cardamom pods lightly. Reserve some lemon juice for the tomato-cucumber side, and divide the salt between chicken and rice to taste. Chili is an optional extra, not included in the shopping list.
steps: Ahead or 0:00 — Marinate. Mix chicken with 300 g yogurt, garlic, ginger, ground spices, some of the measured salt and lemon juice, reserving the rest for rice and serving. Refrigerate 30 minutes to overnight; keep raw chicken cold.

0:30–1:10 — Infuse oil, brown onions, cook eggs and rice. Heat the measured oil in a wide Dutch oven. Add the cinnamon, cracked cardamom, whole cloves and bay leaves for 30–60 seconds to infuse the fat (release their aroma into the oil); lift them out before they darken and reserve. Caramelize the onions (cook them slowly until deeply golden) in the scented oil, working in batches; reserve half the onions. Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook until both whites and yolks are firm; timing depends on egg size and starting temperature, then transfer immediately to cold water to stop the cooking; peel when cool. Rinse basmati; parboil (partly boil) in salted water until about 70% cooked, with a firm centre, then drain.

1:10–1:35 — Cook chicken. Return the reserved whole spices to the Dutch oven with the marinated chicken and remaining onion. Cook over medium heat, stirring, until the chicken is nearly cooked through. Add a splash of water only if sticking.

1:35–2:05 — Dum (steam the layered rice and chicken under a tight lid). Spread partly cooked rice over chicken. Top with reserved onions and cilantro. Cover tightly; cook at very low heat 20–25 minutes, then rest 10 minutes. Check chicken reaches 74°C and rice is cooked; add a few spoonfuls of hot water and steam longer if needed.

Serve. Remove the cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and bay leaves you can find. Halve the eggs over portions; check that the whites and yolks are firm. Dice cucumber and tomatoes; season with lemon and serve separately with remaining yogurt.

title: Butternut Squash Turkey and Bulgur Skillet
preparationGuidance: The squash amount is the raw peeled, deseeded flesh: buy it prepared, or obtain enough whole squash to weigh this amount after peeling and deseeding. No whole-to-peeled yield is assumed. Cook bulgur with water according to its package. Pumpkin seeds are an optional extra, not included in the shopping list.
steps: 0:00–0:12 — Start bulgur and dice. Cook bulgur according to package. Weigh the raw peeled, deseeded squash and cut it into even 1–1.5 cm cubes so it cooks quickly; dice onion and mince garlic (chop very finely). A helper may cube squash earlier that day and refrigerate it.

0:12–0:25 — Brown turkey. In a deep skillet or Dutch oven, cook turkey and onion in oil, breaking up meat. Add garlic and bloom the spices (briefly heat them in the pan to release aroma) for the final minute. Turkey should reach 74°C.

0:25–0:45 — Cook squash. Add squash, 150 ml water and a pinch of salt. Cover and simmer 10–12 minutes, then uncover and reduce (evaporate) the liquid for about 5 minutes. Test a cube with a fork; add a few minutes if needed.
0:45–0:55 — Finish. Fold in spinach until wilted, lemon zest and juice. Spoon over bulgur and scatter pumpkin seeds if using.

title: Honey Mustard Pork with Mash and Green Beans
preparationGuidance: Slice pork into 2 cm medallions. Trim the green beans and cut carrots on the bias. The stock is purchased ready-to-use stock; no bouillon-cube yield is assumed. Add salt and pepper to taste.
steps: 0:00–0:15 — Potatoes and prep. Put salted potato water on high heat. Peel and cut potatoes into even chunks; boil until tender, about 18–22 minutes after boiling starts. Cut pork into medallions (thick, round slices), slice onions, cut carrots on the bias (diagonally), and trim beans.

0:15–0:30 — Sear pork. Sear means brown the surface quickly in a hot pan. Cook pork in a large skillet in batches, 2–3 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate. Cook onions and carrots in the same skillet for 5–6 minutes.

0:30–0:43 — Simmer sauce and beans. Add stock, mustard and honey to skillet. Return pork and simmer gently until cooked to a safe temperature (71°C measured in the centre of each piece, following Health Canada guidance; follow any stricter package directions). Steam or boil beans 5–7 minutes until tender-crisp.

0:43–0:53 — Finish mash. Drain potatoes; mash with butter and warm milk. Make a slurry (cornstarch mixed with cold water), stir it into the pork sauce and simmer until the sauce reaches nappe consistency (a thin, even coating on the back of a spoon). Taste for salt and mustard balance.
Serve. Spoon the pork and sauce over mash, with green beans alongside.

title: Chicken White Bean and Mushroom Stew with Couscous
ingredientLines: 1 tin of tomato paste (156 ml per tin)
preparationGuidance:
Before you start: Soak and fully cook the listed 200 g dry white beans according to their package directions. Use the entire drained batch in this recipe; cooked yield varies. The meal time below excludes soaking and bean cooking. If preparing them ahead, cool promptly and refrigerate until needed.

Use chicken breast or boneless thigh, cut into bite-size pieces. Cook the dry white beans ahead as described below. Use 500 ml water with the bouillon cube, plus couscous cooking water according to its package. Add salt and pepper to taste.
steps: 0:00–0:15 — Chop and brown. Cut onion and carrot into a small dice (¼-inch, about 6 mm cubes), slice mushrooms, then cut chicken separately into even pieces. Brown salted chicken in a Dutch oven in two batches; transfer out.

0:15–0:27 — Build base. Sweat the onion and carrots (cook gently without browning) for 5 minutes, then sauté mushrooms until their water mostly evaporates. Add garlic, tomato paste and herbs for 1 minute.

0:27–0:42 — Simmer. Dissolve the chicken bouillon cube in the water, then add it with the cooked, drained white beans and chicken. Simmer 10–12 minutes until carrot is tender and chicken reaches 74°C. Crush a few beans against the pot to thicken; reduce (simmer uncovered to evaporate liquid) if necessary. This should be spoonable, not soupy.
0:38–0:45 — Couscous in parallel. Pour measured boiling water over salted couscous, cover 5 minutes and fluff.
Finish. Add parsley and lemon. Spoon the thick stew over couscous.

title: Skillet Chicken Rice Bowls with Tomato Cucumber Salad
preparationGuidance: Use whole chicken breasts or boneless thighs. Cook rice with water according to its package. Reserve part of the olive oil for the salad dressing. Yogurt, garlic and dill make the optional sauce and are included in the shopping list. Add salt and pepper to taste.
steps: 0:00 — Start rice and oven. Heat the oven to 200°C. Rinse and cook rice according to the package; let it rest covered.

0:05–0:18 — Prep. Leave the chicken breasts or boneless thighs whole. Pat them dry and season with paprika, oregano, salt, pepper and a little oil. Dice the tomatoes, cucumber and pepper (cut into even cubes), and wash and dry the greens.

0:18–0:35 — Sear and finish. Heat a large oven-safe cast-iron skillet. Sear the chicken (brown the surface quickly in a hot pan) for about 2–3 minutes per side. Transfer the skillet to the oven for a few minutes, checking the thickest piece with a thermometer. Remove it as soon as it reaches 74°C; thicker pieces may need longer. Rest the chicken for 3–5 minutes, then slice it into strips.

Finish. Whisk lemon juice and the reserved olive oil for the salad. If using the optional sauce, stir yogurt with grated garlic and dill. Fluff the rice, dress the salad (toss it with the lemon dressing), and serve with the sliced chicken and sauce.
